guides.body: Integration roadmap Use this roadmap as an execution checklist. The idea is to start with a first manual call, validate the expected behavior, and only then bring the flow into your application's code. guides.title: Overview
guides.description: Understand the integration architecture, environments, endpoints, and response pattern of the idCerberus API
guides.body: Overview The idCerberus API brings together digital onboarding, KYC, data enrichment, biometrics, fraud prevention, risk analysis, and compliance services. The integration was designed to support both complete onboarding flows and single shot queries by CPF or CNPJ. How it all fits together Before diving into endpoints, tokens, and payloads, it's worth understanding three pieces that repeat throughout this documentation. For each one: what it is, why it exists, and what it's for in your implementation. Service 1. What it is: a specific query or check, like "CPF status at the Brazilian Federal Revenue" or "compare a selfie with a document." It has its own code ( SERVICE SOMETHING ) and returns an isolated result. 2. Why there are more than 300: each type of data or check becomes a different service, because each company uses a different combination of them. You never need all of them. 3. What it's for: it's the unit you actually call. Every implementation starts by deciding which services solve your problem. See [Choose the right service](/en/guides/escolha o servico certo). Single shot query vs. onboarding 1. What it is: two ways to use a service. Single shot means calling a service on its own, right away, directly through POST /api/service api . Onboarding means combining several services into a guided journey, with steps, captured fields, and a final status ( APPROVED , IN PROCESS , REFUSED ). 2. Why both exist: not every need is a full registration. Sometimes you just need to confirm one piece of data (single shot); sometimes you need to guide the user through an entire KYC flow (onboarding). 3. What it's for: it defines the integration model you'll build. If the answer is "just confirm one piece of data right now," that's a single shot query via API. If it's "register the user from scratch, with a document and a selfie," that's onboarding via SDK or Web Client. The webhook is the same mechanism for both paths. See [Webhooks](/en/guides/webhooks) to set it up. Pr...

guides.title: Authentication
guides.description: Generate JWT tokens and authenticate protected calls to the idCerberus API
guides.body: Authentication Use this flow to generate the JWT token used in protected calls to the idCerberus API. Authentication is the first step before consuming onboarding, individual services, business services, or customer operations. Access credentials consist of client and secret , provided in advance by React IT. If you don't have these credentials yet, contact us by email at [contact@react it.com](mailto:contact@react it.com). Our team can guide you through creating an account and getting the access you need for API integration. What it is, why it exists, what it's for 1. What it is: the step that turns client + secret into a short lived access token (JWT) that your application uses in every protected call. 2. Why it exists: client and secret are long lived credentials. If they leak, the damage is permanent until they're rotated. The access token expires within minutes, so even if it leaks, the risk window is small. That's why day to day calls use the token, not client / secret directly. 3. What it's for: it defines a piece of your application's infrastructure, something in your back end that generates and renews the token automatically, so the rest of your code never has to worry about it. No. Generate a token and reuse it until it expires ( expires in ). Generating a new one for every call works, but it wastes an extra call per request. The call returns an authentication error (401). Generate a new token and repeat the original call. See [Status and errors](/en/guides/status e erros) for the full handling. No. They're different credentials per environment. A staging client / secret doesn't generate a valid token to call production, and vice versa. guides.title: Onboarding via SDK
guides.description: Generate a TokenOnboarding, track registration status, and download the final report
guides.body: Onboarding via SDK Use this flow when the user's data capture happens through the idCerberus SDK. Your company's back end generates a tokenOnboarding , hands that token to the app integrated with the SDK, and then queries the result processed by the backoffice. The tokenOnboarding identifies the registration through the entire cycle: creation, execution in the SDK, processing, result query, and PDF report download. Atencao: Don't confuse the two tokens in this flow. access token authenticates your application and expires within minutes (see [Authentication](/en/guides/autenticacao)). tokenOnboarding identifies a specific registration and stays valid throughout the whole process, even after the access token expires. If the access token expires mid flow, generate a new one. The tokenOnboarding doesn't change. What it is, why it exists, what it's for 1. What it is: a component (mobile or web) provided by idCerberus that captures the user's document, selfie, and data directly on their screen, following the onboarding script configured for your product. 2. Why it exists: capturing a document and biometrics with enough quality for validation (focus, lighting, angle, liveness) is a problem already solved by the SDK. Reimplementing this from scratch is expensive and error prone. 3. What it's for: your application doesn't process images or implement a camera; it just generates the tokenOnboarding , hands it to the SDK, and then reads the result already ready. If your use case is just querying data (without capturing the user's document), you probably don't need the SDK. See [Choose the right service](/en/guides/escolha o servico certo). When to use it Use this integration when you need to: 1. start an onboarding flow in a mobile app or web experience integrated with the SDK; 2. send documents or initial data to support the registration; 3. query status, captured fields, and services run; 4. download the final PDF report for audit or storage purposes. guides.title: Webhooks
guides.description: Get automatic notifications when an onboarding changes status, without polling
guides.body: Webhooks Use webhooks to have idCerberus notify your application when an onboarding changes status, or when a single shot query finishes processing, instead of your application having to keep asking (polling). What it is, why it exists, what it's for 1. What it is: a URL of your application that idCerberus calls automatically ( POST ) every time an onboarding's processing changes status. 2. Why it exists: querying GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding} in a loop until the status leaves IN PROCESS works, but it burns calls and delays your application's reaction. The webhook flips this: you're notified the moment there's news. 3. What it's for: it's the recommended way to track onboarding in production. Reserve polling (see [Onboarding via SDK](/en/guides/onboarding sdk)) for when the webhook isn't configured yet, or as an occasional check. Info: Configuring the webhook (URL and security key) is currently done by the React IT team, it's not self service via the API. Request activation at [contact@react it.com](mailto:contact@react it.com), providing the URL that should receive the calls. How it works 1. Something relevant happens: an onboarding changes status (goes from IN PROCESS to APPROVED or REFUSED ), a manual review decision is made, or a single shot query in POST /api/service api finishes processing. 2. idCerberus builds the content (the same format as GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding} , adapted when the source is a single shot query). 3. idCerberus makes a POST with that content to the URL configured for your product. 4. Your application responds with success ( 2xx ) to confirm receipt. Info: The webhook isn't instantaneous in a strict sense. Automatic onboarding processing is checked every few seconds and fires when it finds a change; a single shot query fires the webhook about 10 seconds after the HTTP response. A manual review decision (someone approves/rejects through the backoffice) fires right away. None of these times are a contractual ...

guides.title: FAQ
guides.description: Direct answers to the most common integration questions, organized by topic, before opening a ticket
guides.body: FAQ This page brings together, in one place, the questions that come up most often during an idCerberus integration. The idea is simple: before opening a support ticket, look for your question here. A good share of reported "bugs" are expected behaviors that just weren't clear in the technical documentation. Nota: Use Ctrl + F (or Cmd + F on Mac) to search for a keyword on this page before going through the sections manually. Authentication and token No. Generate an access token at POST /api/token generate and reuse it until it expires, according to the expires in field in the response. Generating a new one for every call works, but it wastes an extra call per request. You get HTTP 401. Generate a new token with client and secret and repeat the original call. This is a real HTTP status, different from service permission failures that also show up as "401 in the body" (see the status section below). No. They're different credentials per environment. A staging client / secret doesn't generate a valid token to call production, and vice versa. The databases and the authentication realm are physically separated between the two environments. This pair is released by React IT along with the contracted product, it's not something you generate yourself. Request it by email at [contact@react it.com](mailto:contact@react it.com). Single shot query (POST /api/service api) Yes, and it's the number one source of confusion in this API. POST /api/service api almost always returns HTTP 200, even when the query failed completely. The real reason lives inside the body, in status.code and status.message . Never decide success or failure based only on the HTTP status. A real HTTP 401/403 only happens due to an authentication problem (missing, expired, or wrong environment token), and the call doesn't even reach service processing. "Product not enabled for the service" and "inactive product" don't generate HTTP 401/403 on this endpoint: the call returns HTTP 200 with the problem describe...

guides.body: Common integration errors Use this page when a call fails, returns empty, or looks different than expected. guides.title: Integration best practices
guides.description: Recommendations for integrating the idCerberus API securely and reliably
guides.body: Integration best practices Use these recommendations to reduce failures, avoid exposing credentials, and get your integration ready for production. Credentials and token Practice Reason Generate the token in the back end Avoids exposing client and secret Don't put client and secret in the front end Users could inspect the credentials Don't version credentials in Git Avoids accidental leaks Renew the token when it expires The token has limited validity Don't log the full JWT The token can allow protected calls Environments 1. Use staging for development and testing. 2. Use production only after validating the flow. 3. Don't mix a staging token with the production URL. 4. Don't mix a production token with the staging URL. Environment Base URL Staging https://backoffice hml.idcerberus.com Production https://backoffice.idcerberus.com Requests 1. Always send Content Type: application/json on requests with a JSON body. 2. Always send Authorization: Bearer {jwt token} on protected calls. 3. Validate required fields before calling the API. 4. Send CPF/CNPJ in the format expected by your flow. 5. Use a timeout on HTTP calls. Retry Use retry only when it makes sense. Situation Retry? Timeout Yes, with a limit Temporary network failure Yes, with a limit Expired token Generate a new token and repeat Invalid payload No Service without permission No Invalid CPF/CNPJ No Responses 1. Don't use only the HTTP status to decide business success. 2. Also read status.code and status.message . 3. Handle a status.code other than 200. 4. Save externalId when it's returned. 5. Remember that a negative result isn't necessarily a technical error. Example: Logs Record useful information for investigation, but without exposing sensitive data. guides.title: Glossary
guides.description: Common terms used in the idCerberus API documentation
guides.body: Glossary This page explains common terms used in the guides and the API Reference. Term Meaning API A way for one system to talk to another system through requests Endpoint A specific URL that runs an operation Request A call sent to the API Response The response returned by the API HTTP method The type of operation, like GET or POST Header Information sent along with the call, like authentication or content type Body The content sent in the request, usually in JSON JSON The data format used in the API's examples Base URL The environment's starting address, like staging or production HML The staging environment, used for testing Production The environment used for real queries Token A temporary code used to authenticate calls JWT The format of the authentication token returned by the API Bearer The authentication type used in the Authorization header client The application identifier used to generate a token secret The application secret used to generate a token service The field that defines which product runs in POST /api/service api CPF Individual taxpayer document CNPJ Business taxpayer document result The object with the data returned by the service status.code Technical processing code status.message Technical processing message externalId External query identifier, when returned OCR Extracting data from documents via image Webhook An automatic notification idCerberus sends to your URL when an onboarding changes status id cerberus token The header sent in every webhook call, used to confirm it came from idCerberus FaceMatch Facial comparison between two images Liveness Proof of life validation KYC Customer knowledge and validation process PEP Politically exposed person Practical example In this request: service tells the API which product to run, and cpf tells it which person to query. In this header: Authorization is the header, Bearer is the authentication type, and {jwt token} is the token generated by the API.

guides.title: About the OCR Service API
guides.description: Practical guide to choosing, configuring, testing, and interpreting OCR services in POST /api/service-api.
guides.body: Use this page to integrate OCR services through POST /api/service api . It shows which service to use, how to build the payload, what the return should look like, and what to check before opening a ticket or touching your implementation. Basic requirement: the token needs to belong to the correct product, and the product needs to have the service active with the API enabled. If the product setup is incomplete, the call can authenticate and still return an access failure. Info: SERVICE OCR can be processed by different partners depending on your product's configuration. This usually doesn't change what you do in the integration, but it can occasionally vary one specific result field (for example, the recognized document type). Treat the contract as "the fields on this page usually come like this," not as a rigid field by field guarantee. Use SERVICE OCR when the document is an RG, CNH, OAB, RNE, or PASSPORT and the payload has documentType . Use SERVICE OCR CNPJ CARD to extract the CNPJ and OCR text from the CNPJ card. Use SERVICE OCR PROOF OF ADDRESS for bills, invoices, and accepted proofs. Use SERVICE OCR EMANCIPATION for variable documents with no fixed layout. Fastest test If you just need to validate the call in staging, start with the ready made examples: Ready made curl with SERVICE OCR , documentType: CNH , and image1 . Ready made curl with SERVICE OCR , documentType: RG , image1 , and image2 . Ready made curl for SERVICE OCR CNPJ CARD with a CNPJ card image. The full technical catalog, with every field and example for each service, lives in [Individual Services](/en/guides/servicos pessoa fisica) and [Business Services](/en/guides/servicos pessoa juridica). Use them as the reference source when you need a service's full contract. CPF, registration, score, compliance, and complementary data services. CNPJ, business registration, business owners, risk, and compliance services. OCR, face, liveness, document analysis, and image payloads. Scores, validations, compliance, certificates, and risk signals. How to use this page 1. Choose the service family. 2. Copy the service code or confirm the calling alias configured for the product. 3. Open POST /api/service api in the API Reference. 4. Select the corresponding example. 5. Map the expected response. Consumption pattern Every product on this page uses the same call base: The service field picks the product. The other fields vary by query: document services use images or URLs, PF services use cpf , PJ services use cnpj , and some certificates require extra data like uf , rg , or court . Atencao: The API validates service against the services enabled for the client's product. Because of this, in some cases the value sent in the call can be a short product alias, not another alias documented in the catalog. Before testing with the client, confirm the alias for the product, copy that value into the body, and then fill in the required fields for the chosen family.
